model_facts.attention: hybrid linear attention with periodic sparse attention layers

lines.name: staging
lines.detail: 8 cores + 32 GiB, CPU only, to its own timeout

lines.name: verification
lines.detail: 4 cores + 16 GiB, CPU only, to its own timeout

lines.name: storage
lines.detail: 306 GiB for 0 day(s) plus 4 billed after deletion

cost_envelope.covers: Accelerators, the CPU and memory billed alongside them, the staging and verification containers, and volume storage including the period Modal bills after deletion.
cost_envelope.does_not_cover: Cold starts triggered by requests that reach the platform. A web server function is scheduled before any code in the container runs, so a request allocates accelerators first and is refused second, including after the deployment expiry. With proxy auth on, only a holder of a workspace token can do this and the refusal takes seconds. With a public endpoint anyone can, without limit, and no figure here bounds it.
notes: The accelerator term is priced against the deployment window, not the container timeout, because a request arriving after a container exits simply starts another one. One container timeout is added so a container starting just before the expiry is still covered.
Volume storage keeps billing after the GPUs stop, and Modal bills deleted data for up to four days, so both are included.

memory_fit.caveat: Advertised VRAM against an approximate checkpoint size. Passing this check does not prove the model serves at the requested context length; no official hardware requirement for GLM-5.3-Flash was published on the model card or in https://github.com/zai-org/GLM-5 as of 2026-08-30.

endpoint.credential_handling: The API key is stored in a Modal Secret and injected into the serving container as an environment variable. Only the secret name and the variable name are ever recorded.

blockers: Modeled cost $48.22 exceeds the planning threshold $10.00.
warnings: Proxy auth is on, so Modal rejects unauthenticated requests at its edge before scheduling a container and they cannot allocate accelerators. A request bearing a valid workspace token still cold-starts a container, including after the expiry, where it is refused within seconds. That residual is operator-controlled and is not priced above.

steps.name: setup
steps.purpose: Authenticate the local Modal CLI against your workspace.
notes: Opens a browser and writes a token to ~/.modal.toml.

steps.name: secret
steps.purpose: Store the endpoint API key as a Modal Secret so the serving container receives it as an environment variable.
notes: Export GLM_SELFHOST_API_KEY in your shell first; the generated command references the variable and never contains the value.
Creating the secret in the Modal dashboard instead keeps it out of shell history entirely.

steps.name: volume
steps.purpose: Create the persistent volume that will hold the weights.
notes: Creating an empty volume is free; storing weights on it is not. Storage bills until the volume is deleted.

steps.name: stage-weights
steps.purpose: Download the pinned model revision onto the volume using CPU and network only, then write a manifest of what landed.
notes: No GPU is attached to this step. Weights are never downloaded on an accelerator.
This transfers hundreds of GiB and takes a long time; the cost is CPU container time plus the storage it leaves behind.
Re-running with the same revision is a no-op once the manifest matches.

steps.name: verify-weights
steps.purpose: Re-check every staged file against the manifest, on CPU, and record the result the serving container requires.
notes: CPU only. No accelerator is allocated to find a truncated download.
The serving container refuses to start until this has passed for the revision it is configured with.

steps.name: manifest
steps.purpose: Print the staging manifest recorded on the volume.
notes: CPU only, seconds of container time.

steps.name: deploy
steps.purpose: Deploy the serving app and obtain its https URL.
notes: Deploying registers the app. GPUs are allocated on the first request and released after the scaledown window.
Every budget parameter is read from the environment at deploy time; the app refuses to build if any is missing.

steps.name: health
steps.purpose: Liveness probe. Cheap, bounded, no model work.
notes: The first authenticated call cold-starts the container and therefore allocates GPUs.

steps.name: readiness
steps.purpose: Readiness probe: the model list is only served once weights are loaded.
notes: The header references a shell variable, so the command text never contains the key.

steps.name: smoke
steps.purpose: One bounded chat completion proving the endpoint serves.
steps.command: curl -fsS --max-time 120 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -H "Authorization: Bearer ${GLM_SELFHOST_API_KEY}" -d '{"model":"zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash","max_tokens":16,"stream":false,"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Reply with the word: ready"}]}' '<deployed-url>/v1/chat/completions'
notes: Capped at 16 output tokens so a misbehaving server cannot generate indefinitely.
This proves the endpoint works. It is not a benchmark: timing evidence comes from the collector step.

steps.name: collect
steps.purpose: Measure the endpoint with the existing LLMTraceFX API collector, which owns all timing evidence.
steps.command: llmtracefx-optimizer collect-api --run-id glm53flash-selfhost-smoke --provider modal-selfhost --endpoint '<deployed-url>/v1/chat/completions' --model-id zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash --prompt-file examples/optimizer/api-smoke-prompt.txt --output-dir output/glm53flash-selfhost --api-key-env GLM_SELFHOST_API_KEY --request-timeout 120.0 --model-revision 03eb5366286afd40d2221b1d9c63a6dd1ba4832e
notes: Metrics are produced outside the server on purpose: the server does not measure or grade itself.

steps.name: stop
steps.purpose: Stop the app so no container can be started by a request.
notes: Do this first during teardown; it is what stops GPU spend.

steps.name: delete-volume
steps.purpose: Delete the weights volume so storage stops accruing.
notes: Storage is the charge that outlives the experiment. Modal bills deleted data for up to four days after deletion.
Skip this only if you intend to serve again soon; re-staging means transferring the whole checkpoint again.
